text: The Shattering was a great war in the Lands Between's past that destroyed the established order and eventually gave rise to an abomination.
During the Shattering, the Elden Ring's timeline split, giving rise to the new branching dimension in which Nightreign takes place.
The Shattering encompasses not just the ring's breaking but also the subsequent wars in which demigods, each bearing a Great Rune, fought across the Lands Between.
It was the war of the Shattering that eventually drew forth the Night Lord.

A nameless former knight, defeated in battle during the Shattering and struck down by a hero, crawled out from under a pile of corpses and awoke to curse the world beneath a dark, rainy sky, becoming the Primordial Night Lord.
Heolstor is identified as the first Night Lord, as the word 'primordial' means original or ancient.
Over time the power of the Night spread from Heolstor to other beings, creating additional Night Lords.
A text at the Round Table Hold's underground crypt states that the 'condemned of the first nightfall' bear a sin too great for absolution and are fated to guide their progeny until the night breaks.

The ancient souls in the Round Table Hold's crypt were laid to rest as part of a ritual meant to draw their descendants there in anticipation of the coming threat of the Night, as explained by the Iron Menial.

The Primordial Night Lord's Rune text states that the Cutting-Gifted Tribe foresaw the coming night and planned for many moons to prevent it, concluding their only chance was to cheat a god, having glimpsed the sin of the Erdtree and being punished for their trespass.
The Cutting-Gifted Tribe's punishment was not exile or death, but an eternal duty to prevent the coming of the Night.

Before the Golden Order's dominance, the world that became the Lands Between existed in a primordial state called the Crucible, where living things were interconnected without fixed hierarchy or identity.
The Greater Will, an outer god, imposed the Elden Ring as a new law, bringing the Golden Order, sites of grace, and the promise of near-immortality, displacing the Crucible's fluid order.
Pre-catastrophe Limveld was a civilization structurally similar to the Lands Between, with an earth tree-like structure, sites of grace, roads, cities, and Golden Order hierarchies.
The Night Lords were either drawn to Limveld or created specifically for it, because Limveld's cosmological structure made it uniquely vulnerable to them.
Pre-catastrophe Limveld's civilization was not weak or foolish, but was structurally brittle due to being built entirely on principles of order, making it vulnerable to forces of disorder.
Ruins most thoroughly marked by Gladius's influence are the oldest, representing the earliest stage of the civilization's collapse.
Ruins shaped by Libra's influence are layered on top of Gladius-era ruins, representing a slightly later stage of the collapse.
Maris's presence is evident in underground spaces and coastal areas where the sea has encroached far beyond natural limits.
Equilibrian's marks are the most recent and widespread, adding irresolvable opposition on top of the destabilization caused by the other Night Lords.
The catastrophe that created modern Limveld unfolded gradually across multiple stages rather than as a single event, and in some sense continues into the game's present.

The first stage of Limveld's catastrophe was cosmological: the Greater Will's attention and golden light grew less consistent, causing sites of grace to flicker, initially dismissed as maintenance issues.

The second stage of Limveld's catastrophe was biological: Crucible-aspected flora and fauna began reappearing in civilized areas, and the civilization's response of stricter containment proved insufficient.
The third stage of Limveld's catastrophe was the arrival or full manifestation of the Night Lords, who exploited rather than created the world's existing vulnerabilities.
As Limveld's catastrophe progressed, roads stopped being maintained, cathedrals were abandoned, and sites of grace went dark as their connection to divine attention became unreliable.

Under Libra's influence, Limveld's civilization developed courts and religious institutions that became mechanisms for producing verdicts and enforcing compliance rather than pursuing justice or wisdom.
The Forsaken Hollows' severance from grace is tied to the destabilization of Limveld's connection to the Greater Will's divine infrastructure as Night Lord influence deepened.
Environmental evidence suggests the Round Table Hold's evacuation in Limveld was connected to an escalation of a Night Lord's influence that outpaced the hold's ability to provide safety.

The pre-catastrophe civilization built roads throughout the world believing in its own long-term future and investing in infrastructure meant to serve generations, which it would eventually be unable to maintain.
The Shattering in Elden Ring was caused by the Night of the Black Knives, when assassins killed Godwyn the Golden, prompting Marika to shatter the Elden Ring.
The Iron Menial was originally a cog of war before being modified for housekeeping duties, which failed, leading to him being discarded and later awakening at the Round Table.
Wilder and the Duchess's mother was afflicted by the Night during childbirth, which could only be removed by her death; the Night's affliction then passed to the Duchess.
The Duchess once left on a journey, and enough time passed that Wilder forgot her face and name before the Night later massacred their tribe, leaving Wilder as the sole survivor.
The Guardian's homeland was attacked with cursed blades that severed the Pinion Folk's wing joints, permanently preventing them from flying.
In Elden Ring lore, the Night of the Black Knives saw Godwyn the Golden killed by Black Knife Assassins at the same moment Ranni slew her own flesh, splitting their bodies and souls.
Ranni destroyed her body but preserved her soul in a doll, while Godwyn lost his soul but kept his body, which mutated into a creature in the Deeproot Depths.
The rune of death, stolen from Maliketh and imbued in the Black Knife Assassins' blades, spread corruption across the lands, creating deathroot.
Long ago, the White Horn ruled the western waters while the Black Claw ruled the eastern seas, and the two became rivals vowing to duel one day.
The Northern Croft Manor was a wealthy household known for making puppets before the Night invaded and killed everyone inside.
The Menial later notices the Night Shard pointing in a direction and recounts a legend of a beast that devoured soldiers during a conflict between two realms.
The Witch of the Wheel reveals that the Recluse's infant grew into a creature that devoured armies and even consumed the Witch herself, leaving the Recluse the sole survivor.
The Executor existed in the Lands Between before the Erdtree's destruction and the fall of the Golden Order caused by the Night.
Upon returning the retrieved items, the Executor experiences a flashback showing the Erdtree intact before the era of the Round Table.
Gladius was driven out of its wolf pack due to its abnormal three-headed birth.
Gladius once bit and stole a man's sword, but the man showed no fear, impressing the wolf.
The man raised Gladius, who remained loyal to him ever after, always carrying the man's sword.
When the Night's influence reached Adel's territory, it killed off all its prey, leaving it starving and eventually driving it mad.
Noster's lore states the duo's original forest habitat was consumed by surrounding desert, forcing them to flee and band together.
Fulgor was once considered the left arm of the gods he served but was betrayed and maimed by his companions, losing that arm.
Caligo noticed a calamity from its mountain, likely the rise of the Night Lord, and descended to investigate.
